newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currencies end down as U.S. assets gain.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currencies end down as U.S. assets gain.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures ended moderately lower as the dollar gained with U.S. assets.
March marks and Swiss led the currency declines after each slipped to contract lows in Globex trading on Monday.
"It was pretty much one way -- dollar up -- I guess," one IMM floor manager said. He reported a sale of 3,000 March marks on the close. "Other than that, it was spotty trade all the way around."
Traders noted Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony before the U.S. Senate harbored no surprises, further boosting the dollar.
Greenspan was upbeat on the U.S. economy, while warning of risks of wage-driven inflation.
The central bank chief, in his testimony to the Senate banking committee, also called the rise in the U.S. stock market "breathtaking."
With no surprises from Greenspan, traders said the dollar continued its uptrend against key currencies.
"We're starting to see some corporate interest to buy dollars, maybe because they felt they were missing the boat," said Ralph Delzenero, vice president foreign exchange marketing at First Chicago.

"What we've seen is corporate interest, and fundamentally there just doesn't seem to be a new reason" for the dollar's gains versus the mark, Delzenero said. He said fundamentals for weak marks have been in place for some time, with the market just now catching up to those levels.
"I don't think anything has really changed here, the market is just catching up," Delzenero said.
The IMM trading floor manager agreed. "Germany is in weak economic shape and raising rates is nowhere near on the horizon," he said.
March marks closed above their $0.6154 contract low.
Further support lies at $0.6148, another trader said.
March yen also ended down after a visit to new contract lows in Globex trade early this week, but trade was choppy there much of the day, a floor source said.
March yen made new session lows late Tuesday, then rebounded slightly from there.
March Canadian dollar trade was lackluster much of the day, then surged briefly late. Traders said an uptrend was firmly in place in Canadian dollar, with upside targets of $0.7550.

At settllement, March yen closed down $0.000073 at $0.008538, marks were off $0.0062 at $0.6161, Swiss francs were down $0.0122 at $0.7090, sterling was down $0.0082 at $1.6610, Canadian dollars rose $0.0011 to $0.7509, and Australian dollars were down $0.0023 at $0.7779.
